# Independent browser search witness

**HOLD pending restored-build independent green.** Frozen browser driver SHA-256 `68c55e48ba8740715248dc5d3c0577e0db1c30fe414d15ba7adbbb031f56f1ef`; original v6 application patch `00f6d9164e6844f9aefa35e60c730dea19f7ae4394c3fcae2750611cfc67fb42`; controlled default-endpoint mutant patch SHA `2f46644f1b3143f8d09f3bddf630efa28b3d4efbd6f0eeeb6b7c2a7c7cbe0f1b`. Root-built mutant result reports exit 0 with search source SHA `ca084c47673c0a8a808dda84eda8b8521e39db95154e66fdfa53cf6fdbe6c94f`; `serve.json` SHA `5b2372fe3f32afacff98cec52d882d940c0d9472f4d65ba6af9b2753d40160d7` has no rewrite. I verified both hashes immediately before the independently run probe.

Using qualified Bun 1.4.4 SHA `0a2237cdcfa0d16ef501d9acca9f0026309ef348bea7393a64e8d1e3609565cc`, empty environment with qualified Node PATH, the frozen driver and Chrome Headless Shell 157 executable SHA `ed0e3d67ce3cc2528acb7290ebe86181c144890ff7f610e86268317c6139d518`, the actual browser red exited 1 at `search-result`. It requested `/api/search`, followed HTTP 301 to `/api/search/`, received 404, and had ready document, query `construct`, zero options and no loading indicator. Previously requested HTML, scripts, styles and brand assets returned 200, there were no blocked page requests or browser exceptions, and direct browser and server children exited 0. The search assertion timed out after these recorded settled states; the recorded 404 and UI state, rather than timeout alone, establish the behavioral failure. Actual result SHA `d7589941ba8b1c0317d414108d3f1ccccec117d9982c837f94a614e4485be0d9`; log SHA `001f381b3a7d92bd2903f433fb7aeb24d6de4bb9bda1427e2fc434f2b2f5e10b`. Original installed Chrome Page.navigate failure and initial mutant setup StopIteration are retained separately and are not behavioral reds.

The source and output are owned by root and must be restored/rebuilt there. Await root confirmation of exact restored source/output before executing this same frozen driver for an independent green. Root's diagnostic-v8 fixed-source result is not a substitute for that independent run. CDP interception restricts observed page requests, not an OS-level browser network sandbox; direct-child exit alone does not certify every Chrome descendant reaped. This does not prove deployment, production host behavior, visual baseline parity, or full S6.

## Restored independent green and focused source closure

**KEEP the direct static search witness on restored v6.** After root's restored build/type/HTTP receipt recorded all three actual exits 0 and 21 source hashes, I reran the identical frozen driver and qualified Bun/headless browser against the frozen parked worktree. `independent-green-v1/result.json` reports actual exit 0 and all 14 checks: `/api/search.json` 200 JSON, actual `construct` result, unrelated query with zero results, real result navigation, direct nested reload and title, home/back/forward, no captured runtime/hydration exceptions or blocked page requests. Recorded local asset responses were 200 or 304; the redirected document was 301 then 200. Browser/server direct children report exit 0. Green result SHA-256 `74e1b9e595bbe6fc81c6d495fab853710c82ee6db4e84175773ad39502365815`, log SHA `4aa6b290a078d74a6c1f84210b5f94def66f9645396e26507adbab54deeda7aa`, browser version JSON SHA `ce120e056ba6378792bb6268f6b250b52ba39e57e74daa75806d849898670e34`. All 21 receipt-bound source files independently rehashed after the probe with zero mismatches (`independent-source-after.txt`).

After both probes, `/bin/ps` succeeded and a filter limited to executable names under the owned headless-shell package or Chrome commands referencing the two unique profiles found no matching processes (`independent-postrun-processes.txt`, SHA `d8af46d3207626a6faa6f83f9acae589b14a724ab234a2e5d0573f3f1465a775`). The first attempted `/usr/bin/ps` path did not exist and its piped placeholder was invalid; it was discarded and replaced with the checked `/bin/ps` result. This is an OS process snapshot of those explicit identifiers, not proof of general OS network containment or a process-tree audit beyond them.

Focused source review: `useDocsSearch` explicitly sets the actual generated `/api/search.json` and `serve.json` no longer relies on an extensionless rewrite. The local HTTP oracle requires 200/JSON/index membership and ultimate 404 for old and nearby paths, as well as the established unknown HTML status/body; the observed browser red/green supports the client routing change. The Vite pre-adapter removes `lang.js` only for collection `meta.json` requests and delegates resolution with `skipSelf`, preserving other modules; this is a focused static review, not an independent review of all build output or security findings. The installed Fumadocs `StaticOptions.from` supports this path. No new source/test edits, build, full suite or public deployment were made here. Root's host/provider metadata and local output do not establish that this unmerged source is deployed or that the production host has been exercised; no production/S6 completion claim follows.

security.text:
# Independent SECURITY closure: frozen docs static v6

Decision: **KEEP for the three original security findings, on the exact frozen v6 source.** This is a narrow closure review, not a new whole-application audit, production deployment claim, or approval to merge the original jackin PR. I made no source, test, configuration, authentication, browser, build, or PR mutation.

## Binding and evidence read

The reviewed patch is `author-patch-e1fb608-v6.patch`, SHA-256 `00f6d9164e6844f9aefa35e60c730dea19f7ae4394c3fcae2750611cfc67fb42`, on base `e1fb608b12ba5cb812460c49bc79b05103f4b270`. I read `author-file-hashes-v6.json`, including its separate `direct_static_search_targets` binding for `docs/src/components/search.tsx` SHA-256 `4215f4eaa2cd4d160a682693d8384c95ffdddf80991ec389087ed8e5f6a6df56`. The publishing worktree at `wt/jackin-docs-static-publish-20261109` matches the recorded hashes for the source files examined; the parked `wt/docs-full-static-01a1b218` carries the restored public output. I compared the original independent SECURITY and CODE HOLD reports, the current GitHub Pages/CNAME metadata receipt, the restored build/type/HTTP receipt, and the independent actual browser red/green witness.

## Original findings

1. **Serving contract — CLOSED for the intended static artifact, with deployment explicitly unclaimed.** `useDocsSearch` now sets Fumadocs' official static `from` option to `/api/search.json`, and the generated public tree contains the real `api/search.json` file. `serve.json` contains no rewrite or catchall. The current production host is identified as GitHub Pages by the repository Pages API (`build_type=workflow`, source `main` `/`, HTTPS) and the domain CNAME to `jackin-project.github.io`; the output includes standard `index.html`, `404.html`, `.nojekyll`, and CNAME artifacts. The local HTTP oracle requires 200/JSON/index membership at the direct path and ultimate 404 for the old extensionless path and a nearby path. The independently witnessed old default endpoint requested `/api/search`, redirected, returned 404, and failed the real result; restored source requested `/api/search.json` with a real hit/miss and navigation. These facts remove the host-specific rewrite dependency. They do not show that this unmerged source has been deployed or that the new artifact was requested from production.
2. **Destination containment — CLOSED for this build path.** `build-static.ts` rejects symlinks in `content`, `public`, and `.source` before `postInstall` or Vite's public copy, rechecks `.source` and `public` afterward, creates a private `mkdtemp` stage, rejects symlinks in emitted public output, and checks each generated parent using `lstat` and `realpath` under the staged public root before exclusive `wx` writes. Lexical destination validation and duplicate/collision checks remain. The restored output has no symlink. Same-user concurrent filesystem replacement is outside the demonstrated local build isolation; no untrusted shared output directory or such race was identified in this frozen scope.
3. **Unknown-route oracle — CLOSED.** `check-static-output.py` now requires an unknown HTML URL to return 404 with HTML media and the exact established `/404` document body. It separately requires missing Markdown and OG paths to return 404, and old/nearby search aliases to end in 404. The root's restored build, type, and public HTTP commands each report actual exit 0 on unchanged frozen source, with 31 source pages. The independent browser witness reports the causal red on the obsolete endpoint and green on the direct JSON endpoint with no captured hydration or runtime exception.

## New boundary delta and limits

The Vite pre-plugin applies only to `meta.json` collection requests carrying `lang.js`, removes that query marker, and delegates to Vite resolution with `skipSelf`; it does not introduce a runtime server route, dependency fork, fallback endpoint, or broader alias. The browser entry imports public page data and browser collections, while the inventory and OG modules are built into the private stage. A bounded static scan of the 7.7 MB restored public tree found no symlink and no JS asset containing `inventory.server`, `og.server`, `node:fs`, `process.env`, or `.source/`; this is supporting evidence, not a formal proof of every transitive browser import. No new HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW security finding was identified in the reviewed delta.

Before publication, retain exact v6 source/hash binding and the independent public oracle/browser and graph receipts on the final committed tree. The current host metadata establishes the platform, while actual deployment behavior of this new unmerged artifact remains unobserved. This review does not waive required project gates, visual approval boundaries, or the operator's PR merge authority.

http-oracle.text:
# Independent public HTTP oracle retention

**KEEP for the clarified not-found text-identity contract.** This receipt reconstructs the independent review from retained artifacts after the originally cited report was found absent; it does not assume how that happened. No tests were rerun for this receipt. The original oracle SHA-256 was `b11d0794dd493ee8c31adfc13cad0f7dd5f489a9d8c926cb6fec062800d6e56c`; the corrected oracle is `c1cb2eb4d96a6e069a9cf38e3f00e95359f4ee364dde7c83a9bdd7bf36a66615`. All referenced artifact hashes are recorded in `independent-receipt-hashes.txt`; exact mutant file hashes and exit codes are in `control-results.json`, `control-404-v3.json`, and `common-404-result.json`.

The original independently run, isolated public HTTP oracle rejected four single-output controls at meaningful assertions, each exit 1: valid wrong-page HTML at `wrong title /developing/construct-image` (`wrong-page.log`); changed anchor text at `anchor content missing /developing/construct-image` (`missing-anchor.log`); a removed referenced JS file at `missing client asset` (`missing-asset.log`); and a removed page ID in otherwise valid search JSON at `search index missing /developing/construct-image` (`missing-search-id.log`).

The first 404 status/body controls, including v2, edited the root fixture `serve.json`, but the actual `serve` resolves `--config serve.json` relative to `.output/public`. Those runs passed because the mutations did not affect the consumed server configuration; they are ineffective fixtures, not causal witnesses. The corrected v3 controls changed only the actual `.output/public/serve.json`: wrong unknown-route status was rejected as `unknown HTML status was 200, expected 404` (`wrong-404-status-v3.log`), and a differing `/404` reference body was rejected as `unknown route did not serve the not-found document` (`wrong-404-body-v3.log`), both exit 1. The latter establishes a comparison mismatch check only, not independent semantic correctness of a shared body.

A separate actual counterexample exposed that distinction: replacing only generated `404.html` with the valid home page made both `/404` and the unknown route serve the same wrong home body. The original oracle accepted it with exit 0 (`common-404-result.json`, `both-404-bodies-wrong.log`) because it compared those two shared responses. After restoration, `restored-inventory.json` showed zero byte differences against the frozen parked source over 196 generated output files and 40 content files, with oracle/package/root config also compared; final original-oracle `green-final.log` reported success. The later common-body control restored `404.html` to the same recorded original SHA `b2ceb8f105bec596adefb439de988cf486e516f15454a22710b6fef93581b7c1`.

The independently witnessed corrected oracle rejects that exact retained home-page substitute at the semantic `/404: wrong not-found title` assertion, exit 1 (`../independent-http-oracle-v2/corrupt-refusal.log`); after restoring the original 404 output, the same public CLI passes, exit 0 (`../independent-http-oracle-v2/restored-good.log`). The unchanged earlier asset, page, search and 404 comparison assertions retain their original causal controls; they were not rerun after the small oracle change. The v2 `independent-verdict.md` records the witness and identified a possible overbroad visibility claim. The separate `scope-clarification-addendum.md` records the orchestrator's final decision: the accepted HTTP-parser contract is title and heading **text identity**, not computed CSS/HTML visibility. Script/style/comment content is excluded; visual rendering remains a browser concern.

This is a scoped local public-oracle retention decision. It does not establish deployed production behavior, visual-baseline parity, full S6 or release qualification. No source edit, additional test or rerun occurred in reconstructing this missing receipt.

not-found-oracle.text:
# Independent not-found oracle fix witness

**KEEP the demonstrated common-wrong-body regression control; HOLD a claim that the oracle proves headings are visible.** Reviewed only the oracle change `b11d0794dd493ee8c31adfc13cad0f7dd5f489a9d8c926cb6fec062800d6e56c` -> `c1cb2eb4d96a6e069a9cf38e3f00e95359f4ee364dde7c83a9bdd7bf36a66615`. Existing status/media/body comparison and unrelated asset/search/content checks remain in source. Added HTMLParser collects decoded title and h1/h2 text across nested markup, excludes script/style/comment text, and normalizes whitespace; public 404 and unknown route both require the literal source-approved title and headings.

Isolated copy from previous witness; the unmodified old oracle independently accepted the exact common-home substitution (v1 `common-404-result.json`, exit 0). With the frozen corrected oracle and the **same** home HTML SHA `f6c7a1ff026ba6c95523bf072bc0d1ea80efe05ef9e0f6244280c98f8a50a1b5` replacing only generated `404.html`, the public CLI exits 1 at `/404: wrong not-found title` (`corrupt-refusal.log`, SHA `f0069eefe07e6b66abd14cec9bf01f53a6318e617fa036c124721f2d53e48570`). This is the intended semantic refusal, not setup or parse error. Restored original `404.html` SHA `b2ceb8f105bec596adefb439de988cf486e516f15454a22710b6fef93581b7c1` and exact oracle SHA above; same CLI exits 0 (`restored-good.log`, SHA `cdb78269f279781aeb5201e8fbd7d7271f319b7928b65a47f2a17c165f4b4aa8`). Prior source-bound wrong status, unequal 404 bodies, missing asset, wrong page and missing index controls remain applicable because their assertions were not changed; those controls were not rerun in v2.

**Remaining static limit:** `Document` excludes script/style content, but does not check `hidden`, `aria-hidden`, `display:none`, hidden ancestors or browser-computed styling. Thus a document with hidden matching headings can satisfy this text-identity check while not visibly showing them. The actual restored 404 displays the intended headings; this review did not run a new hidden-heading test. Do not claim the checker verifies heading visibility solely from this implementation. If the independently approved visible-heading requirement is strict for all inputs, this is a remaining plan mismatch; otherwise specify the narrower textual-identity contract. The root was notified. No app source, production assets, builds, or production server changed; no deploy or full S6 claim.

scope-clarification.text:
# Not-found HTTP oracle scope clarification

The orchestrator defines the accepted HTTP parser contract as semantic title and heading **text identity**, not CSS/computed visibility or support for hidden/aria-hidden ancestors. Under that clarified scope, KEEP the independently witnessed common-home false-negative closure in `independent-verdict.md` on oracle SHA `c1cb2eb4d96a6e069a9cf38e3f00e95359f4ee364dde7c83a9bdd7bf36a66615`. The previous approved-plan use of “visible” was broader than this intended HTTP contract; this addendum does not rewrite the plan or witness. Script/style/comment exclusion remains part of the textual check. Actual restored page has the expected title and headings; no source change or hidden-heading test was performed. Actual CSS/browser rendering and visual parity, and production deployment of this unpublished source, remain separate and unclaimed.
